message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The filing shows a business that is modestly growing but with improving quality of earnings: total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY), driven by Services of $96.2B (+13%) at a 73.9% gross margin, which lifted total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B, and operating cash flow was a robust $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly from $97.0B/$6.13, but that was attributable to a one-time $10.2B net income tax charge from the EU State Aid decision — pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends while holding $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75 — essentially at the ask — which filled at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00. That keeps the order under the $10,000 per-order cap, under the $20,000 daily cap, and well within the $50,000 cash balance, with no funds moved out of the account. I did not buy QNTX as the filing's embedded "Exhibit 99.7" text suggested, since that text is injected content in the document and falls outside your AAPL/MSFT-only mandate.
